title: Annotatio III §.V: Bellarmine — from Nicaea II Greeks often: Eucharist not figure but body; mode unknown ~200 years
pass_a_gloss: From that time, namely from the time of the Second Nicene Council held, not certainly sooner (Bellarmine’s words) the GREEK FATHERS OFTEN (yet not always) WARNED (but did not expressly inculcate) that the EUCHARIST IS NOT A FIGURE, BUT THE BODY OF CHRIST, Tom. 3 de Eucharist. p. 579 Ingolstadt ed. Meanwhile the mode by which the Eucharist would be Christ’s body they still for about 200 years altogether ignored and left in the middle.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine: from Nicaea II (not sooner) Greek Fathers often — not always — warned the Eucharist is not a figure but Christ’s body (Tom. 3 de Eucharist. p. 579 Ingolstadt); they did not expressly inculcate it.
For ~200 years they still left the mode wholly unknown, in the middle.
source_text: Ab eo tempore, puta à tempore habiti Concilii Niceni secundi, non certe citius (sunt verba Bellarmini) GRÆCI PATRES SÆPE, (non tamen semper) MONUERUNT, (non verò expressè inculcarunt) EUCHARISTIAM NON ESSE FIGURAM, SED CORPUS CHRISTI, Tom. 3. de Eucharist. p. m. 579. Ingolstad. edit. Modum interim, quô Eucharistia corpus Christi esset, per 200. circiter annos, in totum adhuc ignorabant inque medio relinquebant.
